steps.text:
This is worse in some ways:
- Giant arm joint at top-right huge cropped, base/arm not in view coherently; it's too close because shoulder at (0.95,.54,.42) is near camera. And gripper part at center-right floats (the palm). We only see arm pieces at frame right edge, disconnected. Looks bad.
- Cup now larger, good, but composition is sparse and weird; giant circle top right.
- Table is extremely dark and empty; napkin looks like a flat orange rectangle (too bright due spotlight), spoon.
- Lighting is dim, cup lacks definition.
- The robot's shouldered arm is way too close because camera is near base. Need move camera away or arm further.

Fundamental issue: first-person camera located near robot arm means arm is huge. We need either:
A) Camera farther from arm base, with telephoto lens (narrow FOV) so cup stays large and arm normal. E.g. camera at (1.6,1.2,2.4), FOV 28, cup at (0,.1,.2) distance 2.6, cup 0.19/(2*2.6*tan14)=14.6%, still small. Move cup closer to camera? cup z .8, distance 1.8, fov 35 => 17%. Hmm.
B) Make the robot arm much smaller scale (e.g. 0.6x) relative to cup, like a small desktop robot. Then it won't dominate. But physical scale with huge cup might look odd; could be a toy robot. Yet POV of a small robot, cup is giant; first-person would make cup large. Not required realism.
C) Don't show arm base/shoulder; use a wrist-mounted first-person camera. Then arm geometry in front (gripper) is manageable. This is the earlier idea and likely cleaner. Camera attached just behind gripper, sees two fingers and cup. No giant links. The arm itself need not be visible. This reads clearly first-person robot. Could show a bit of wrist/forearm at bottom edge. It avoids all framing issues. I think this is the right choice.

Let's switch to wrist camera. Then camera and gripper rigidly tied: define tool frame with cup target and camera behind W. The gripper fingers are at ±x around cup, camera behind at z+ (relative to forward d) looking along d. Cup appears centered, fingers enter from lower-left/right. This is visually strong and intimate. We can still show arm blur in background? No.

Wrist POV composition:
- tool frame origin T at cup center; d downward/forward approach. Camera at T - d*0.55 + up*0.08, looking at T. Fingers at T. Cup fills 30-40% frame, fingers visible each side. Table and background around.
- At start, camera farther back? If camera fixed relative gripper, cup size changes as arm moves away: camera is 0.55 behind T; cup distance 0.55 always, so cup constant. But T is offset from cup at start (hover above), cup smaller/farther. If camera at T - d*.5, and cup is T + offset, distance can vary. At grasp, cup center =T, cup 0.19 at .45 => 40% frame. At start T above/right, cup .4m away from T =>1m =>20%.
- G ripper fingers around T; at start open, cup not between them yet. Good.

We need design T trajectory from start (above/right of cup) to grasp. Camera moves with T and orientation d. Start d mostly downward but tilted. Cup visible below.

This is essentially a drone/wrist cam view. It will show the gripper approaching the cup, closing, lifting. No full arm. We can add a curved forearm housing behind camera at frame edges? Camera behind the gripper; some wrist body could be visible at very bottom (behind camera impossible). But we can mount camera above wrist looking forward-down; a small portion of wrist housing and cables could be at bottom. Add a "camera housing" mesh near camera in front view? No, camera can't see itself. We can add the gripper base (palm) in view at bottom behind fingers. Yes palm is behind T; camera further behind, sees palm and fingers. Good.

Place camera at local z=-0.30? ToolGroup local z forward. Palm at z=.12, fingers .14-.38, T at z=.27. Camera should be at z=-0.05 or -0.15 (behind palm) looking forward, so palm may block view. Put camera above palm at y .12 and z -.10, looking down slightly. It sees top of palm at bottom, fingers extending forward. The cup is at z .27. Nice.
- camera local (0, .10, -.18), look at (0, -.03, .30), FOV 58.
- But if camera inside toolGroup and toolGroup orientation downward, camera looks down. Cup centered.
- The palm at z .118 is between camera and cup; palm height .105, camera above .10, so top of palm visible at bottom, fingers at sides. Good.
- Wrist flange at z 0 behind palm. Camera at z -.18, just behind wrist; flange could be under camera.
- Camera direction relative to d: look at local (0,-.03,.30) means slight down angle 16°. Vertical composition cup occupies center.

World layout can remain table scene, but arm base/links irrelevant. Remove or scale down? In wrist view, camera follows T; background will show table, slat wall, maybe shelf, but arm base at (.95,.42) might be in frame to the right during early approach, huge. We should remove base/arm links or put them behind camera. Since camera is at wrist near cup, base is 1m to the right/back, likely out of frame if camera looks down at cup. At end camera is near (.05,.5,.3) looking down/forward; base at .95,.42 is 0.9m to right, might be visible at right edge but not giant. Could hide the pedestal and upper links entirely for the wrist POV, except maybe if background. But "机械臂" needs the gripper to read as robot arm. We have fingers/palm. Add a wrist joint and a bit of forearm entering from top/bottom edge, but camera attached there. The camera can see the forearm behind? Since camera is mounted on the wrist top looking forward, the forearm behind is out of view; maybe top edge shows forearm. Not necessary.

Better: Wrist camera at back of gripper, we see the whole gripper (palm + fingers). The gripper itself is enough mechanical context. Add cable details and orange accents, maybe an LED ring on palm top.

This solves composition and makes cup hero.

We can avoid by moving the camera to align with the jaw axis more, or orient the jaw perpendicular to the camera view exactly so both fingers are equidistant and outside the silhouette.
